Current evidence does not support purchasing amber-tinted glasses for all 400 staff. The 3-week trial has critical limitations. While the glasses group improved slightly more (0.4 points) than the control group (0.3 points), the difference is negligible and statistically unreliable given the design flaws. Both groups improved similarly, suggesting other factors influenced sleep. Proceeding with a full rollout would be premature. A larger, randomized, double-blind trial controlling for shift patterns is necessary before investing in equipment for all night-shift staff.

We recommend expanding the trial to control runner variables and collect cross-team hit rate data before deciding on organization-wide adoption. Current results are inconclusive.

Recommend running a properly designed randomized controlled trial before investing £X,000+ in glasses for everyone.
